acceptance: The hard-stop bound is decided by the owner and the code, tests and docs all state and meet it.
context:

description:
## Problem
The run hard stop fires 30 s after the limit (`HARD_STOP_GRACE_SECONDS = 30.0`, `benchbox/utils/run_deadline.py`). `hard_stop` (`benchbox/cli/run_time_limit.py`) only then runs `cancel_remote_work()` (which can wait up to the 25 s cleanup window, `graceful_cleanup_window_seconds()`, if cleanup had not already started at the limit), the partial-result export, `RunDeadline.stop_children` (SIGTERM, 0.2 s, SIGKILL) and `end_descendant_processes()`, and exits 124. The docs promise an exit bound: site `docs/reference/cli/run.md` says "The hard bound is therefore the limit plus 30 seconds"; site `docs/usage/data-generation.md` says BenchBox "writes that result and exits"; `_project/decisions/run-timeout-2026-11-20.md` decision 15 says the test shows exit within the limit plus 30 seconds. The test in `tests/unit/utils/test_process_group_term_ignoring_children.py` (#4446) actually asserts `< limit + HARD_STOP_GRACE_SECONDS + 2.0`. So "exits by limit + 30 s" is not guaranteed; "starts stopping at limit + 30 s" is.

## Change
Ask the owner which contract holds, then make code, tests and docs (BenchBox `docs/operations/run-safety.md`, decision 15 of the decision record, and the site pages above) say the same thing. If the owner wants an exit bound, budget remote cleanup, export and the kill wait inside the 30 s instead of after it.

## Decision gates
- STOP and ask the owner (choice dialog): exit bound (process gone by limit + 30 s) or start bound (stopping starts at limit + 30 s, with a stated exit bound). Quote the answer verbatim on this item.
- No new default timeout anywhere, and no deadline check inside a query timer.
- Do not shorten the 25-second remote-cleanup window without the owner's decision.

## Verification rubric
Pass: docs and decision record state the chosen bound in the owner's words; two subprocess tests, one with a SIGTERM-ignoring child and one whose remote cleanup never returns, assert the chosen bound exactly (exit bound: `elapsed < limit + 30.0`; start bound: the hard stop begins at `limit + 30.0 ± 0.5` s and the documented exit bound holds), passing 20 repeats on macOS and in `make ci-linux`; existing hard-stop and remote-cleanup tests pass.
Fail: docs and behaviour disagree, or a test needs an unexplained margin.

## Guardrails
Work in a linked worktree (`make worktree-create`), never the primary clone. Edit files with the edit tool, never by script. Heavy work (benchmarks, test tiers, UAT, generators at scale) only through `make heavy-run` or lock-taking entry points; never skip the lock, admission or watchdog; never delete anything under `~/Developer/benchmark_runs`. No live cloud run and no cloud credentials unless this item's Decision gates say the owner approved it in the current task. BenchBox imposes no default run limit: add none. No comments or docstrings in first-party code; one changelog fragment for a user-facing change. Never post a stand-in review, close and reopen a pull request to restart CI, use `--no-verify`, force-push, or rewrite an author. Arm once; a second time only after fixing the cause the refusal named. Reply on every review thread; resolve it only after the bot's review of the new head does not raise it again. Never end processes that the test runner owns; tests signal only processes they started and still own.
